paper_metadata.title: Quantum Amplitude Loading for Rainbow Options Pricing

summary: The paper implements a gate‑based quantum algorithm for rainbow option pricing using Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation and evaluates two amplitude‑loading strategies (integration and direct) on a 24‑qubit IBM QASM noiseless simulator with 1000 shots. For a two‑asset option (strike $190, maturity 250 days), the quantum estimates match the classically computed payoff of $23.0238 within the IQAE confidence interval (ε=0.01, α=0.05). The work demonstrates a full circuit construction but only at toy scale.

experiments.description: End-to-end gate-based quantum rainbow option pricing using Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with two alternative exponential amplitude-loading implementations (integration and direct) on a noiseless IBM QASM simulator for a two-asset, real-data example.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for rainbow option pricing
algorithm.convergence_criteria: IQAE run with precision ϵ = 0.01 and confidence interval α = 0.05

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two Gaussian-distributed log-return registers (2 qubits each) are prepared, correlated via a Cholesky-based affine transformation, then a maximum module is applied in return space; payoff is encoded into the amplitude of a target qubit using a comparator plus either direct or integration-based exponential amplitude loading.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected discounted payoff of a rainbow call option, with payoff max(M_t - K, 0) where M_t is the maximum asset price at maturity; implemented via delayed transition to price space and amplitude estimation of the payoff expectation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator on z >= (log(K)-b')/b selects between constant branch and exponential-loading branch; no QUBO/penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Two-asset rainbow option pricing example with real-world market data, strike K = $190, maturity 250 days, and correlated log-returns.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical daily log-returns are used to estimate means and covariance; Gaussian discretization uses two qubits per asset; arithmetic rounded to one decimal place; Cholesky decomposition used to correlate standard Gaussian samples; transition to price space delayed until payoff calculation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 1000 shots on IBM QASM noiseless simulator; measured objective qubit after IQAE; compared estimated payoff against classically computed expected value including discretization and arithmetic precision.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load Gaussian distributions, apply affine transformation via Cholesky factor, compute maximum in return space, comparator against threshold, and prepare exponential amplitude-loading branch.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Post-process IQAE estimate using the derived scaling relations to recover expected payoff; discounting is performed classically.

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude Estimation vs Monte Carlo sampling for expectation estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is asymptotic/theoretical; no empirical wall-clock speedup is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Amplitude estimation gives quadratic improvement over classical Monte Carlo, i.e. O(1/M) sampling convergence versus O(1/sqrt(M)) classically for estimation accuracy.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(M)) sampling convergence for Monte Carlo estimation

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; analysis only discusses asymptotic quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not quantified; experiments use only 24 qubits and two assets with extremely coarse discretization (2 qubits per Gaussian).
limiting_factors: Only quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation
Very small problem instance (2 assets, 2 qubits per Gaussian)
State preparation and arithmetic overhead dominate circuit cost
No empirical runtime comparison with classical Monte Carlo

notes: The paper reports the IBM QASM noiseless simulator, 1000 shots, and a total of 24 qubits.
No explicit circuit depth, gate counts, or transpiled depth are reported for the experiment; only analytical T-depth formulas are given in the complexity section, so those fields are left null.
The paper explicitly states the quadratic sampling advantage of amplitude estimation over classical Monte Carlo.
Authors discuss theoretical quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation but do not claim experimental quantum advantage.
Experiments are validation-only simulations of a small toy instance.

experiments.description: Rainbow option pricing using IQAE with the direct exponential amplitude loading method on the IBM QASM noiseless simulator (separate implementation path evaluated alongside the integration loading method).

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation with direct exponential amplitude loading
algorithm.key_difference_from_exp_1: Uses direct exponential amplitude loading circuit (controlled rotations + MCX) instead of integration-based loading.

key_results: Estimated payoff shown in Figure 5 with confidence interval overlapping the classical reference value of $23.0238
Executed with 24 qubits and 1000 shots on the IBM QASM noiseless simulator
